text:
support: FYI customer 'AcmeCorp' opened an escalation — p99 latency on /v1/chat jumped ~2x since the 14:05 deploy in us-west-2. They report timeouts and a few 500s. Not a billing issue, looks performance/oom related.

matt: digging in metrics now. cluster-wide p95 up ~30%, p99 doubled. I can see a cluster of OOM events on node gpu-rt-07 around 14:12 UTC and a flurry of fallbacks to smaller model variants.

rachel: logs? can you paste the OOM lines and KV sizes?

matt: pasted snippets below — exact timestamps from runtime logs.
```
[2026-03-14T14:12:58Z] ERROR model-serving: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory (requested 314572800)
[2026-03-14T14:12:58Z] WARN allocator: fragmentation ratio=0.72 held=21.8GB mapped=24.5GB
[2026-03-14T14:12:58Z] WARN kvcache: entries=1_120_432 size_bytes=25_187_392_000 high_watermark=93% growth_rate=+1.3%/min
[2026-03-14T14:12:59Z] INFO runtime: fallback activated -> model-redwood/REDUCED@v2 for request routing
[2026-03-14T14:13:02Z] ERROR runtime: request latency p99=2.8s (baseline 1.1s)
```

kevin: that kvcache size looks like the culprit — per-node KV growth combined with allocator fragmentation. Could be long-lived sessions storing large prefixes + no TTL eviction.

lisa: are OOMs causing the long tail or are we hitting slow paths during fallback? both would explain p99.

matt: it’s both — when model-server fails allocation, we spawn CPU fallback which is slower; meanwhile allocator doesn't release fragmented reserved memory immediately causing repeated cudaMalloc failures until process restarts.

rachel: immediate mitigation checklist (suggested):
- enable customer-level routing to smaller variant (done automatically for some but enable for this customer)
- reduce max_batch_tokens and max_batch_size for problematic queue to limit peak allocations
- trigger KV cache eviction on affected nodes (evict LRU to target ~8GB)
- recycle the model-server process on gpu-rt-07 to recover fragmentation quickly
- enable jemalloc background_thread / aggressive purge on next deploy

matt: running commands now — will throttle traffic for that service and evict cache.

# commands I'm running (for transparency):
```
nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,used_memory,process_name --format=csv
kubectl -n inference exec pod/gpu-rt-07 -- curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8080/admin/kv/evict -d '{"policy":"lru","target_bytes":8000000000}'
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deployment/model-server --field-selector metadata.name=gpu-rt-07-model-server
```

kevin: I'll open an infra ticket to check for possible CUDA driver regression and node-level memory fragmentation. If a node restart is needed, coordinate with oncall.

lisa: i'll inform customer: ETA ~30-45m for mitigations (throttling + eviction + restart). i'll include repro steps and what we're doing.

matt: quick repro steps for devs to reproduce locally (useful for a fix):
1) run the load generator with concurrent sessions of long prefixes:
```
go run ./tools/loadgen -qps 120 -concurrency 40 -model redwood/large -prefix-file test/long_prefixes.txt
```
2) watch KV growth in admin endpoint: `curl http://localhost:8080/admin/kv/stats`
3) repeatedly allocate large tensors until you see `cudaMalloc failed` in logs.
```
# example admin output
{"entries":1120432, "size_bytes":25187392000, "evictions":1245}
```

rachel: longer term actions we should track:
- add soft TTL and size caps per customer for KV entries (prevent single customer bloat)
- drop-in allocator tuning: enable aggressive background purging and reduce fragmentation (jemalloc MALLOC_CONF: background_thread:true, dirty_decay_ms:1000,muzzy_decay_ms:1000)
- expose per-model KV budget and autoshrink policy in console and routing rules
- better graceful degradation: seamless async spill-to-disk for oversized KV or early reject with clear client error instead of fallback slowdown

kevin: logging action items: infra ticket #INF-6321 for node health, runtime task RT-441 for jemalloc tuning and KV quotas, product task PM-990 to expose KV budgets in console.

matt: status update — evict call returned success, KV size dropped to ~8.1GB on gpu-rt-07, restarting model-server now to clear fragmentation.

ops-bot: Restart initiated for deployment/model-server on gpu-rt-07 by matt at 2026-03-14T14:29:12Z.

lisa: customer notified at 14:30 UTC, said they'd pause heavy traffic for 30m. keeping channel updated.

matt: post-restart p99 down to ~1.25s in the affected queue, p95 back to baseline. still watching for re-growth; i'll keep an automated eviction every 10m as a stopgap for next 2h.

rachel: thanks — assign RT-441 to me and matt. we'll prototype jemalloc flags and a KV per-customer soft budget by next sprint.

kevin: i'll follow up on infra ticket and post if we need physical node replacement.

lisa: closing loop with customer once stable. :white_check_mark:

support: tagging this thread in case SRE/infra need to reference logs. summary for handoff: transient GPU OOMs caused by KV cache bloat + allocator fragmentation -> fallback to CPU creating p99 tail. mitigations applied: KV eviction, throttling, process restart. follow-ups: jemalloc tuning, per-customer KV budgets, better spill/early-reject UX.
